newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rights group criticises Palestinian death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Rights group criticises Palestinian death penalty.

text.p: A U.S.-based rights group has criticised the Palestinian Authority's decision to impose the death penalty against Palestinians who sell land to Jews.

Human Rights Watch's criticism came on the heels of Washington urging Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to uphold the rule of law and warning it would condemn any official backing of retribution against Arabs selling land to Jews.

In a statement faxed to Reuters on Friday, Human Rights Watch said it had written Arafat demanding he retract an announcement by Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen of a death penalty against people selling land to Jews.
"Human Rights Watch believes that imposing the death penalty as proposed violates internationally accepted norms and principles of human rights," the letter sent to Arafat said.
Palestinian officials were not available to comment.

Human Rights Watch said it understood that commercial land purchases by Israelis and land confiscations by the Jewish state were used by the Israeli government to lay claim to Palestinian lands occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.
But it said that methods of resisting such actions "must be consistent with international human rights standards, including the right to life".
An Israeli court on Thursday ordered the detention of two Palestinians allegedly involved in the murder of an Arab Israel said was killed for selling land to Jews.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Thursday condemned the killing as "a savage murder" and urged the Palestinian Authority to apply the rule of law.
Abu Medeen was quoted in a published report 12 days ago as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.
